title: Abandonment of senior citizens - the criminal liability explained
p1:
A parent spends years caring for a family. But what happens when that same parent is left helpless in old age?

Many people think neglecting an elderly parent is only a moral failure. The law may treat it as a crime too.
p2: A lesser-known fact is that abandonment of a senior citizen is not just a family dispute. Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, leaving a senior citizen without care when it places their safety or well-being at risk can attract criminal liability.
p3:
The offence can lead to punishment, including imprisonment and fine. The law aims to protect elderly parents and senior citizens who are unable to support or care for themselves.

The practical lesson is simple: financial support alone is not always enough. Respect, care, and protection are also responsibilities that cannot be ignored.
conclusion: Do you think stronger legal action can reduce the abandonment of senior citizens, or does the solution need to begin with family values?
